experiments.name: high-unroll load-to-ALU chain
experiments.command: ./bench --unroll 100000 --iters 100 --warmup 10 --reps 7 --init 'addi.d $r20, $sp, -1024; li.d $r4, 8; st.h $r4, $r20, 0; li.d $r4, -8; st.h $r4, $r20, 8' --asm 'ld.hu $r4, $r20, 0; slli.d $r4, $r4, 48; srai.d $r4, $r4, 48; add.d $r20, $r20, $r4'
experiments.notes: L1D hit, load-to-ALU latency 4 cycles. The unsigned result is explicitly sign-extended with slli/srai so the base pointer can alternate +8/-8; chain_latency subtracts 2 shift cycles and 1 add. Measured with unroll=100000.

latencies.notes: L1D-hit load-to-ALU latency is nominally 4 cycles. Re-measured with an ext.w/add.w extension chain: raw 6.06-6.10 cycles, extension-chain baseline 2.19 cycles, giving about 3.9-4.1 cycles. The unsigned extension path adds about 0.1 cycle of uncertainty, so the value is not exactly 4.00 in every measurement. Raw measurement was 4.04; the residual is a systematic +0.03..0.1 calibration offset, so the recorded value is the nominal integer with the observed spread. Raw slope-method measurement was 4.00; the value is 4 cycle(s) and any earlier range was a rounding artifact.

throughput.name: 8 independent lanes
throughput.notes: 8 independent memory operations take 4.00 cycles. Buffer is at $sp-1024.
